subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 1-year-old girl is evaluated for progressive developmental delay and an enlarging abdomen. The liver edge is 5 cm below the costal margin and the spleen 6 cm below it; funduscopy shows a cherry-red spot. Bone marrow aspirate reveals foamy lipid-laden macrophages.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes best explains these findings?
explanation_correct: Progressive neurodegeneration with both a cherry-red spot and hepatosplenomegaly, together with foamy macrophages, points to Niemann-Pick disease. Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes sphingomyelin and cholesterol to accumulate in lysosomes of the reticuloendothelial system and neurons. Unlike Tay-Sachs disease, Niemann-Pick disease enlarges the liver and spleen.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease, which has a cherry-red spot but no hepatosplenomegaly and no foam cells in marrow.
explanation_incorrect.C: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease with hepatosplenomegaly and crumpled-tissue-paper Gaucher cells.
explanation_incorrect.D: Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease, an X-linked disorder with angiokeratomas and renal failure.
explanation_incorrect.E: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy with demyelination, not hepatosplenomegaly.

educationalObjective: Niemann-Pick disease from sphingomyelinase deficiency combines a cherry-red spot with hepatosplenomegaly and foamy macrophages.
